findings.title: website_name not in untrusted_attributes, leaks TL0 website hosts to anonymous viewers
findings.body: The new :website_name attribute is added to the attributes list on line 43 but is not included in the untrusted_attributes macro on lines 105-111, whereas :website is. The whole purpose of untrusted_attributes is to hide TL0 user fields from anonymous viewers (scope.restrict_user_fields? returns true). After this change, a TL0 user with website 'http://example.com/user' seen by an anonymous user will still have website_name='example.com/user' present in the JSON even though website is omitted. Anonymous viewers can now recover the host (and often path) of TL0 users' websites, partially undoing the privacy protection the macro was meant to provide. The fix is to add :website_name to the untrusted_attributes list on lines 105-111, and to update the spec to match.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing ?
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializer invokes include_<attribute>? to decide whether to emit an attribute. The new method is defined as `def include_website_name` (line 153), without the question mark, so define_method for include_website_name? does not exist and AMS falls back to always including the attribute. Every other inclusion method in this file (include_email?, include_stats?, include_suspend_reason?, include_user_fields?, include_topic_post_count?, include_card_image_badge_id?, include_edit_history_public?, include_private_message_stats?) ends with `?`. As written, the inclusion guard has no effect: the JSON always contains website_name (which will be null when website is blank). The method should be `def include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name crashes with NoMethodError if Discourse.current_hostname is nil
findings.body: On line 139, discourse_host is set from Discourse.current_hostname. If that returns nil (misconfigured site, missing host, or specific request edge cases), the elsif on line 144 evaluates `discourse_host.split('.').length`, which raises NoMethodError on nil and 500s the user serializer. The early return on line 140 only guards website_host, not discourse_host. A simple guard like `return if discourse_host.nil? || discourse_host.empty?` (or swapping the logic to compute website data once and using a single safe path) would prevent the crash.

findings.title: URI(website.to_s) is parsed four times in the same method
findings.body: Inside website_name, `URI(website.to_s)` is constructed and parsed four separate times (lines 138, 143, 146, 149). Each call re-parses the URL. The result should be hoisted into a local variable (e.g. `uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil`) and reused for `.host` and `.path` access. This also makes the code easier to read and centralizes the rescue.

findings.title: TL0 anonymous test does not cover website_name, so the privacy regression slips through
findings.body: The untrusted_attributes list at line 11 is `%i{bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background}`. The test on lines 13-15 iterates only over that list, so even if the serializer leaks website_name for TL0 users seen as anonymous, the assertion passes. Combined with the privacy finding above, this means the regression introduced by this PR will not be caught by the existing spec. The list should be extended with :website_name (and a website value should be set on user_profile so that website_name would otherwise be present), so the test enforces the intended privacy boundary.

findings.title: Missing coverage for edge cases of website_name
findings.body: The new examples on lines 77-90 only cover three host-shape scenarios (different domain, identical domain, parent domain). They do not exercise: nil Discourse.current_hostname (currently raises), nil/blank website (include guard relies on the broken method name), URLs whose path is empty ('http://example.com' yields website_host + ''), URLs with query/fragment (e.g. 'http://example.com/u?x=1' drops the query in the displayed name), URLs with ports (host strips port, but path concatenation behaviour should be locked in), and the 'www.example.com vs forum.example.com' second-branch path that is only indirectly covered. Add examples for these so the contract is pinned down.
